Key insight: Sales volume, order count and total revenue move together — these are the strongest relationships in the per-category data, while Average Review Rating shows little or no consistent correlation with revenue or volume.

The chart below illustrates the correlation between category-level metrics: prices, freight, payment value, review ratings, revenue, units sold and order count. It highlights which pairs of metrics tend to increase or decrease together across product categories.

---
{chart_json}

| Metric pair | Relationship (qualitative) | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| Total Units Sold — Order Count | **Very strong positive** | More orders correspond to more units sold; these two are essentially measuring the same demand signal for categories. |
| Total Revenue — Total Units Sold | **Strong positive** | Higher unit volumes drive higher revenue across categories, as expected. |
| Total Revenue — Average Payment Value | **Moderate to strong positive** | Categories with higher average payment per order tend to generate more revenue even at similar volumes. |
| Average Price — Average Payment Value | **Strong positive** | Average product price and average payment per order move together — higher-priced categories have higher payment totals. |
| Average Freight Value — Average Price / Payment | **Weak to moderate positive** | More expensive items often have slightly higher freight, but the relationship is not as pronounced. |
| Average Review Rating — Revenue / Units / Orders | **Weak or no consistent correlation** | Review score does not reliably predict category revenue or volume in this dataset. |
| Average Review Rating — Average Price | **No clear correlation** | Higher-priced categories do not consistently have higher or lower review scores. |

Suggestion: consider asking for a breakdown (e.g., a numerical correlation table or scatter plots for specific pairs like Revenue vs Average Payment Value, or Units Sold vs Average Price) to quantify these relationships and spot category-level exceptions.
